abstract: CNBC reports on workforce transformation plans at JPMorgan Chase and Goldman Sachs, two of the world's largest investment banks. JPMorgan projects that its operations and support staff will decline by at least 10% over the next five years, even as business volumes continue to grow — implying that AI and automation will absorb the workload growth that would previously have required additional hiring. The article examines how major banks are simultaneously reducing operations headcount while aggressively hiring AI and technology talent, reflecting a structural shift in the composition of financial services employment. Goldman Sachs is pursuing a similar strategy, investing in AI capabilities across trading, compliance, and client services while reducing dependency on large operations teams.
keyFindings: JPMorgan Chase projects operations and support staff to decline by at least 10% over five years despite growing business volumes.
The reduction implies AI will absorb workload growth that would previously have required new hires, representing both direct displacement and foregone hiring.
Both JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs are simultaneously cutting operations roles while aggressively hiring AI and technology talent.
The shift reflects a structural change in financial services employment composition from operations-heavy to technology-heavy.
methodology: CNBC reporting based on corporate disclosures, executive statements, and analyst briefings from JPMorgan Chase and Goldman Sachs. Includes internal workforce planning projections shared with investors.
qualifiers: The 10% operations reduction is a forward-looking projection that may not materialize as planned. 'At least 10%' is a minimum estimate from management that could change with market conditions. The article focuses on two elite banks that are not representative of the broader financial services workforce. Growing business volumes assumption depends on macroeconomic conditions remaining favorable.
